root_cause: The refactor in #10012 conflated 'bits per source lane before widening' with 'total bytes read from memory' when deriving the OperandSize for vector-extend loads. The derived size is reused for both bounds checking and instruction emission, so an incorrect (too-small) per-lane size was propagated into the memory-safety-relevant bounds computation instead of being independently fixed at 8 bytes (the true width of the SIMD extend-load instructions on x86-64/AArch64).
findings: The Winch baseline compiler's `LoadKind::derive_operand_size()` computes the `OperandSize` that is passed down into `wasm_load`/`load_impl` to perform the Wasm linear-memory bounds check and emit the actual load instruction.
